findings.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — P2, confidence 100: `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` — The mutex is held through `readWebAssetsFromFile` at line 60, so every development-mode request (which deliberately bypasses the cache at line 45) queues behind disk I/O; concurrent page loads serialize and each additional request incurs the preceding manifest-read latency.

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:40 — P1, confidence 100 — `func GetWebAssets(ctx context.Context, cfg *setting.Cfg, license licensing.Licensing) (*dtos.EntryPointAssets, error) {` — No regression test invokes this cache path concurrently, so a synchronization regression produces no failing test and ships as a data race.

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — P2, confidence 100, `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()`: concurrent production cache misses queue on the mutex but never re-check `entryPointAssetsCache` after acquiring it, so every queued request re-reads the manifest (and makes another CDN request when configured) instead of sharing the first result; a burst of N requests produces N serialized asset loads and request latency.

pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — P2, confidence 100, `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()`: Dev-mode calls always take this exclusive lock and retain it through the complete manifest file/CDN read, so one slow asset read blocks every other request from obtaining assets and queues their handlers behind it.

goldens.comment: The GetWebAssets function implements an incomplete double-checked locking pattern for caching web assets. The function first checks if the cache is populated using a read lock (RLock), and if the cache is empty, it acquires a write lock to populate it. However, it fails to re-check whether the cache was populated by another goroutine while waiting to acquire the write lock.

In addition to the missing double-check, the function has a critical flaw in its error handling: it unconditionally assigns the fetch result to the cache (line 69: entryPointAssetsCache = result) regardless of whether the fetch succeeded or failed. When an error occurs during asset fetching, result is nil, and this nil value overwrites any previously valid cache entry.

adjudication_records.issue_text: pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go:48 — P2, confidence 100: `entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock()` — The mutex is held through `readWebAssetsFromFile` at line 60, so every development-mode request (which deliberately bypasses the cache at line 45) queues behind disk I/O; concurrent page loads serialize and each additional request incurs the preceding manifest-read latency.

adjudication.rationale: The finding correctly identifies that in development mode (cfg.Env == setting.Dev), the cache check at line 45 will be false (bypassed), causing every request to acquire the write lock at line 48 and hold it through the file read operation. This is a valid performance/architecture concern - the mutex is held during I/O which serializes concurrent requests in dev mode. However, this is not a bug per se - it's a design tradeoff for thread safety. The code is correct but has a performance implication in dev mode specifically.
